messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert for customer OrchidHealth (privnet) — significant 5xx spike from backends, NLB healthchecks failing, >80% of requests 502 from edge. Paging @oncall-sre

oncall-sre: I'm on it. Acknowledge. Triage starting — grabbing metrics and NLB health events.

netops-jay: seeing healthcheck 504/timeout from NLB->target group in the privnet account. Target status shows unhealthy across multiple AZs. No security-group changes noted in last 24h.

eng-runtime-ana: Orchid's dedicated pool (dedicated-gpu-orchid) had a config rollout ~1h ago (steady-state kernel updates). Any chance that rollout touched client ports or health endpoints?

se-tilly: Customer reported intermittent DNS failures earlier, but they said it recovered. Could be two independent symptoms.

oncall-sre: timeline: 00:00 alert spike -> 00:10 NLB health failing -> 00:20 increased 502s. I can reproduce 502s hitting their tenant endpoint through the NLB. Running curl from our jump:
```
curl -v --resolve orchid.priv.internal:443:10.20.5.12 https://orchid.priv.internal/health  -I
```
Response: TLS handshake ok, then HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway.

netops-jay: pulled NLB logs — health check responses are 200 from target for /_ping but the NLB health check status still toggles to Unhealthy due to consecutive timeout window. Looking at target group: connection attempts frequently reset.

eng-runtime-ana: checking app logs on dedicated pool — lots of `accept()` failing: "accept: connection reset by peer" and fast restarts of worker threads. Possible ephemeral port exhaustion on the host or upstream proxy rejecting.

sre-lead-omar: Could this be conntrack exhaustion on the customer's NATgw / proxy? Their VPC has a small NAT device for egress and we saw DNS rate limiting earlier. Ask customer to confirm NAT instance metrics.

customer-ops-marks: Orchid confirms they saw NAT instance CPU spikes and high conntrack in the last 30m during a CI job. They're scaling it up now. They also rolled a sidecar proxy in their tenant yesterday.

oncall-sre: mitigation plan — 1) remove NLB healthcheck sensitivity (increase healthy threshold and timeout) to avoid flapping while we stabilize; 2) coordinate with Orchid to scale/replace NAT/conntrack; 3) temporarily route traffic to fallback model / lower capacity pool to avoid full tenant outage. Need approval to change NLB health thresholds (will slightly delay detection).

eng-runtime-ana: I can prepare a canary redirect on the routing layer to send 10% of traffic to fallback variant. That will reduce load on customer's pool.

netops-jay: making NLB change now — increasing healthcheck timeout to 10s and healthy threshold to 4. Patching in 30s. Will monitor.

incident-bot: Deployment approved by @sre-lead-omar; change queued.

oncall-sre: Orchid says NAT scale is started. Any DNS anomalies still?

customer-ops-marks: DNS queries are normal now. NAT scaling looked effective — conntrack usage dropping.

netops-jay: NLB health status: targets moving to healthy after 90s. 502 rate decreased to ~5% from 82%. Latency stable.

oncall-sre: Rolling back sidecar proxy flag? If sidecar created sharp connection churn it's safer to revert. Orchid ops wants us to hold until after validation.

se-tilly: Noting for postmortem: triggers — CI job + sidecar + small NAT instance caused conntrack exhaustion -> upstream resets -> NLB health flaps -> 502 storm.

eng-runtime-ana: Implemented 10% fallback routing and warm-up on fallback. No errors observed.

sre-lead-omar: Good mitigation. Next steps: 1) keep customer oncall loop until 2 hours stable; 2) create incident ticket and schedule RCA with Orchid; 3) recommend hardened healthcheck policy for privnet tenants and guidance doc for nat/conntrack sizing.

customer-ops-marks: Thanks team. Orchids will follow up with NAT instance sizing and disable sidecar for now. Please keep us posted.

oncall-sre: Marking incident as mitigated for now. Monitoring for next 2h; will reopen if regression. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident p1 -> mitigated (5043210145). Pager clear requested.
